pictures.scene: Juan de Valdés Leal, Elijah and the Prophets of Baal — the fire falling on the altar while the prophets of Baal are dragged down at the prophet's word, O LORD, God of vengeance, O God of vengeance, shine forth
pictures.name: pd_valdes_wraak

pictures.scene: Pompeo Batoni, The Fall of Simon Magus — the apostles kneeling in prayer while the magician falls out of the air in front of the emperor, rise up, O Judge of the earth, render a reward to the proud
pictures.name: pd_batoni_rechter

pictures.scene: Gerard van Honthorst, The Mocking of Christ — the grinning men crowding in with the torch and the reed while Christ sits bound under the thorns, how long will the wicked, O LORD, how long will the wicked exult
pictures.name: pd_honthorst_hoelang

pictures.scene: Charles Le Brun, The Entry of Alexander into Babylon — the conqueror carried in on his chariot through the crowd and the trophies, they pour out arrogant words and all workers of iniquity boast
pictures.name: pd_lebrun_roemen

pictures.scene: Jusepe de Ribera, The Martyrdom of Saint Philip — the ropes hauling the old apostle up onto the cross while the soldiers haul and the crowd looks on, they crush Your people, O LORD, they oppress Your heritage
pictures.name: pd_ribera_verdrukken

pictures.scene: Matteo di Giovanni, The Massacre of the Innocents — the soldiers at work among the mothers on the temple floor while the king watches from his throne, they kill the widow and the foreigner, they murder the fatherless
pictures.name: pd_matteo_doden

pictures.scene: Jan Steen, The Dissolute Household — the whole house drinking and wasting while nobody looks up at the basket of judgments hanging over their heads, they say, the LORD does not see, the God of Jacob pays no heed
pictures.name: pd_steen_zien

pictures.scene: Hieronymus Bosch, The Ship of Fools — the boat going nowhere with its crew singing round the hanging loaf, take notice, O senseless among the people, O fools, when will you be wise
pictures.name: pd_bosch_dwazen

pictures.scene: Nicolas Colombel, Christ Healing the Blind — Christ reaching out to touch the blind man's eyes with the crowd pressing round, He who affixed the ear, can He not hear, He who formed the eye, can He not see
pictures.name: pd_colombel_oog

pictures.scene: Albrecht Dürer, Jesus among the Doctors — the boy in the middle of the teachers with their books and their arguing hands, He who admonishes the nations, does He not discipline, He who teaches man, does He lack knowledge
pictures.name: pd_durer_onderwijst

pictures.scene: Adriaen van Ostade, The Alchemist — the old man blowing at his furnace in a room of broken pots with the hourglass running out over his head, the LORD knows the thoughts of man, that they are futile
pictures.name: pd_ostade_ijdel

pictures.scene: Fra Angelico, The Sermon on the Mount — Christ seated on the hillside teaching the disciples gathered close around Him, blessed is the man You discipline, O LORD, and teach from Your law
pictures.name: pd_angelico_tucht

pictures.scene: Vincent van Gogh, Noon – Rest from Work — the two harvesters asleep in the straw with their shoes off and the sickles laid aside, to grant him relief from days of trouble, until a pit is dug for the wicked
pictures.name: pd_vangogh_rust

pictures.scene: Vasily Polenov, The Raising of Jairus' Daughter — Christ taking the dead girl by the hand in the quiet of the room, for the LORD will not forsake His people, He will never abandon His heritage
pictures.name: pd_polenov_verlaat

pictures.scene: Dieric Bouts, The Justice of Emperor Otto III — the widow holding the iron unburnt in her hands before the emperor and his court, surely judgment will again be righteous, and all the upright in heart will follow it
pictures.name: pd_bouts_recht

pictures.scene: Raphael, Saint George and the Dragon — the rider wheeling his horse round and driving the lance down into the dragon, who will rise up for me against the wicked, who will stand for me against the workers of iniquity
pictures.name: pd_raphael_opstaan

pictures.scene: Domenichino, The Guardian Angel — the angel holding the child by the hand and pointing him up toward the light, unless the LORD had been my helper, I would soon have dwelt in the abode of silence
pictures.name: pd_domenichino_helper

pictures.scene: Pieter Bruegel the Elder, The Conversion of Paul — the rider thrown down on the mountain road in the middle of the marching army, if I say, my foot is slipping, Your loving devotion, O LORD, supports me
pictures.name: pd_bruegel_voet

pictures.scene: Rembrandt, The Holy Family with Angels — the mother bending over the cradle in the dark while the angels come down to the child, when anxiety overwhelms me, Your consolation delights my soul
pictures.name: pd_rembrandt_troost

pictures.scene: Gerard David, The Judgment of Cambyses — the corrupt judge taken by the arm on his own seat while his accusers point him out, can a corrupt throne be Your ally, one devising mischief by decree
pictures.name: pd_david_troon

pictures.scene: Caravaggio, The Beheading of Saint John the Baptist — the jailer pointing down to the charger while the executioner bends over the prisoner in the prison yard, they band together against the righteous and condemn the innocent to death
pictures.name: pd_caravaggio_samen

pictures.scene: Joachim Patinir, Landscape with Saint Jerome — the great rock standing over the hermit's cave with the storm out beyond it on the bay, but the LORD has been my stronghold, and my God is my rock of refuge
pictures.name: pd_patinir_rots

pictures.scene: Salomon de Bray, Samson Destroying the Temple of Dagon — the lords feasting on the terrace with their trumpeters while Samson sets his shoulder against the pillar below, He will bring upon them their own iniquity and destroy them for their wickedness
pictures.name: pd_bray_simson

pictures.scene: Aert van der Neer, Nocturnal Fire in a Dutch City — the burning town under an orange smoke-filled night sky with the people standing on the bank, the LORD our God will destroy them
pictures.name: pd_neer_vuur

lines.text: O LORD, God of vengeance,
O God of vengeance, shine forth.
Rise up, O Judge of the earth;
render a reward to the proud.
How long will the wicked, O LORD,
how long will the wicked exult?
They pour out arrogant words;
all workers of iniquity boast.
They crush Your people, O LORD;
they oppress Your heritage.
They kill the widow and the foreigner;
they murder the fatherless.
They say, “The LORD does not see;
the God of Jacob pays no heed.”
Take notice, O senseless among the people!
O fools, when will you be wise?
He who affixed the ear, can He not hear?
He who formed the eye, can He not see?
He who admonishes the nations, does He not discipline?
He who teaches man, does He lack knowledge?
The LORD knows the thoughts of man,
that they are futile.
Blessed is the man You discipline, O LORD,
and teach from Your law,
to grant him relief from days of trouble,
until a pit is dug for the wicked.
For the LORD will not forsake His people;
He will never abandon His heritage.
Surely judgment will again be righteous,
and all the upright in heart will follow it.
Who will rise up for me against the wicked?
Who will stand for me against the workers of iniquity?
Unless the LORD had been my helper,
I would soon have dwelt in the abode of silence.
If I say, “My foot is slipping,”
Your loving devotion, O LORD, supports me.
When anxiety overwhelms me,
Your consolation delights my soul.
Can a corrupt throne be Your ally—
one devising mischief by decree?
They band together against the righteous
and condemn the innocent to death.
But the LORD has been my stronghold,
and my God is my rock of refuge.
He will bring upon them their own iniquity
and destroy them for their wickedness.
The LORD our God will destroy them.
